claim: Amazon RDS uses EBS volumes for database and log storage and, depending on the storage size, stripes across multiple EBS volumes to improve IOPS.
question: What storage hardware does Amazon RDS use?

values.display: EBS volumes for database and log storage

evidence.quote: Amazon RDS uses EBS volumes for database and log storage. Depending on the size of storage requested, Amazon RDS automatically stripes across multiple EBS volumes to enhance IOPS performance.

claim: When an application needs more compute than the largest DB instance class or more storage than the maximum allocation, you can partition the data across multiple DB instances.
question: How do you scale an RDS database beyond the largest instance class or maximum storage?

evidence.quote: If your application requires more compute resources than the largest DB instance class or more storage than the maximum allocation, you can implement partitioning, thereby spreading your data across multiple DB instances.

claim: RDS for Oracle and RDS for SQL Server can add up to three additional storage volumes of up to 64 TiB each, for a maximum of 256 TiB of storage.
question: What is the maximum storage of an RDS for Oracle or SQL Server DB instance with additional storage volumes?

qualifiers.scope: per DB instance, RDS for Oracle and RDS for SQL Server, primary plus additional storage volumes

evidence.quote: For RDS for Oracle and RDS for SQL Server, you can add up to three additional storage volumes, each up to 64 TiB, on top of the primary storage volume to increase the storage capacity to a maximum of 256 TiB.

claim: The FAQ describes General Purpose (SSD) storage with a baseline of 3 IOPS/GB and the ability to burst up to 3,000 IOPS, for moderate I/O workloads.
question: What baseline performance does the RDS FAQ give for General Purpose (SSD) storage?

evidence.quote: With the baseline of 3 IOPS/GB and ability to burst up to 3,000 IOPS, this storage option provides predictable performance to meet the needs of most applications.

note: FAQ wording describes the gp2 model (baseline per GB, burst). The guide (CHAP_Storage, USER_PIOPS.gp3) also documents gp3 with a fixed baseline; numbers lens owns those values. Use this FAQ sentence only with the guide value next to it.

claim: Provisioned IOPS (SSD) storage is optimized for I/O-intensive, transactional (OLTP) database workloads.
question: Which RDS storage type fits I/O-intensive OLTP workloads?

evidence.quote: Amazon RDS Provisioned IOPS (SSD) Storage is optimized for I/O-intensive, transactional (OLTP) database workloads.

claim: With Provisioned IOPS (SSD) storage you specify an IOPS rate when you create the DB instance, and RDS provisions that rate for the lifetime of the DB instance.
question: How does Provisioned IOPS storage deliver its performance on RDS?

evidence.quote: With Amazon RDS Provisioned IOPS (SSD) Storage, you specify an IOPS rate when creating a DB instance, and Amazon RDS provisions that IOPS rate for the lifetime of the DB instance.

claim: Magnetic storage is not recommended for production database instances.
question: Should you use RDS magnetic storage for production?

evidence.quote: Magnetic storage is not recommended for production database instances.

claim: Automated backups enable point-in-time recovery: RDS takes a full daily snapshot in the backup window and captures transaction logs as updates are made.
question: What is the difference between RDS automated backups and DB snapshots?

evidence.quote: The automated backup feature of Amazon RDS enables point-in-time recovery of your DB instance. When automated backups are turned on for your DB Instance, Amazon RDS automatically performs a full daily snapshot of your data (during your preferred backup window) and captures transaction logs (as updates to your DB Instance are made).

claim: The automated backup retention period is 7 days by default and can be set to up to 35 days.
question: What is the default and the maximum RDS automated backup retention period?

qualifiers.scope: per DB instance, automated backup retention period

evidence.quote: Amazon RDS retains backups of a DB Instance for a limited, user-specified period of time called the retention period, which by default is 7 days but can be set to up to 35 days.

note: One sentence states both the default (7 days) and the maximum (35 days); default_or_max is set to default, the maximum is the second display.

claim: By default, RDS turns on automated backups for a DB instance with a 7-day retention period; you do not need to enable them.
question: Do you need to enable automated backups on an RDS DB instance?

evidence.quote: By default, Amazon RDS enables automated backups of your DB instance with a 7-day retention period.

claim: Setting the backup retention period to 0 turns off automated backups, which AWS does not recommend.
question: How do you turn off RDS automated backups?

evidence.quote: If you desire to turn off automated backups altogether, you can do so by setting the retention period to 0 (not recommended).

claim: The backup retention period cannot be set to 0 if the DB instance is a source for read replicas.
question: Can you turn off automated backups on an RDS DB instance that has read replicas?

evidence.quote: The value cannot be set to 0 if the DB instance is a source to Read Replicas.

claim: A point-in-time restore can target any second in the retention period up to the Latest Restorable Time, which is typically within the last five minutes.
question: To what point can you restore an RDS DB instance with point-in-time recovery?

values.display: any second during your retention period

evidence.quote: You can initiate a point-in-time restore and specify any second during your retention period, up to the Latest Restorable Time. You can use the DescribeDBInstances API to return the latest restorable time for you DB instance, which is typically within the last five minutes.

claim: DB snapshots are user-initiated, can be taken as often as you wish, and are kept until you explicitly delete them.
question: How long does Amazon RDS keep a manual DB snapshot?

values.display: kept until you explicitly delete them

evidence.quote: DB Snapshots are user-initiated and enable you to back up your DB instance in a known state as frequently as you wish, and then restore to that specific state at any time. DB Snapshots can be created with the AWS Management Console, CreateDBSnapshot API, or create-db-snapshot command and are kept until you explicitly delete them.

claim: A restore to a point in time or from a DB snapshot creates a new DB instance with a new endpoint.
question: What does an RDS restore from a snapshot or point in time create?

evidence.quote: Please note: When you perform a restore operation to a point in time or from a DB Snapshot, a new DB Instance is created with a new endpoint (the old DB Instance can be deleted if so desired).

claim: During the backup window, storage I/O may be briefly suspended (typically under a few seconds), but there is no I/O suspension for Multi-AZ deployments because the backup is taken from the standby.
question: Is an RDS database available during the backup window?

values.display: no I/O suspension for Multi-AZ DB deployments

evidence.quote: During the backup window, storage I/O may be briefly suspended while the backup process initializes (typically under a few seconds) and you may experience a brief period of elevated latency. There is no I/O suspension for Multi-AZ DB deployments, since the backup is taken from the standby.

claim: RDS DB snapshots and automated backups are stored in Amazon S3.
question: Where does Amazon RDS store automated backups and DB snapshots?

evidence.quote: Amazon RDS DB snapshots and automated backups are stored in S3.

claim: When you delete a DB instance you can create a final DB snapshot, which RDS keeps with your other manual snapshots so you can restore the instance later.
question: How can you keep the data of an RDS DB instance that you delete?

evidence.quote: When you delete a DB instance, you can create a final DB snapshot upon deletion; if you do, you can use this DB snapshot to restore the deleted DB instance at a later date.
Amazon RDS retains this final user-created DB snapshot along with all other manually created DB snapshots after the DB instance is deleted.

claim: The FAQ says automated backups are deleted when the DB instance is deleted and only manually created DB snapshots are retained.
question: What happens to automated backups when you delete an RDS DB instance?

evidence.quote: Automated backups are deleted when the DB instance is deleted. Only manually created DB Snapshots are retained after the DB Instance is deleted.

note: FAQ versus guide: USER_WorkingWithAutomatedBackups.Retaining describes retaining automated backups when you delete a DB instance. The behavior lens owns that guide fact; the conflict queue or the registrar must pair them. Prose should teach the guide behavior.

claim: A DB subnet group should have at least one subnet in every Availability Zone of the Region.
question: How many subnets should an RDS DB subnet group have?

values.display: at least one subnet for every Availability Zone

evidence.quote: Each DB Subnet Group should have at least one subnet for every Availability Zone in a given Region.

claim: Connect to a DB instance by its DNS name, because the underlying IP address can change, for example during failover.
question: Why should applications connect to RDS by DNS name rather than IP address?

values.display: use the DNS Name to connect

evidence.quote: Please note that we strongly recommend you use the DNS Name to connect to your DB Instance as the underlying IP address can change (e.g., during failover).

claim: A common VPC design puts web servers in a public subnet and the RDS DB instances in a private subnet with no internet access.
question: Where should RDS DB instances be placed in a VPC for a public web application?

values.display: private-facing subnet with no Internet access

evidence.quote: You can create a public-facing subnet for your webservers that has access to the Internet, and place your backend Amazon RDS DB Instances in a private-facing subnet with no Internet access.

claim: SSL/TLS encryption of connections is supported for all Amazon RDS engines, and RDS generates an SSL/TLS certificate for each DB instance.
question: Can you encrypt connections to an Amazon RDS DB instance with SSL/TLS?

values.display: supported for all Amazon RDS engines

evidence.quote: Yes, this option is supported for all Amazon RDS engines. Amazon RDS generates an SSL/TLS certificate for each DB Instance.

claim: SSL/TLS encryption is compute-intensive and increases the latency of the database connection.
question: What is the performance cost of SSL/TLS connections to RDS?

values.display: increase the latency of your database connection

evidence.quote: While SSL offers security benefits, be aware that SSL/TLS encryption is a compute-intensive operation and will increase the latency of your database connection.
